analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the speaker, and לָאִשָּׁה identifies the woman as the addressee. וַיֹּאמֶר introduces the quoted question מַה זֹּאת עָשִׂית, “What have you done?”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים לָאִשָּׁה (“Yahweh God said to the woman”), יַהְוֶה names the speaker and אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition. The woman is the addressee.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים לָאִשָּׁה, אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. The singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר identifies one speaker who addresses the woman.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: לָאִשָּׁה identifies the woman to whom God speaks. The reply וַתֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁה (“and the woman said”) names the same participant.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with prefixed preposition לְ and definite article, combined as לָ־.

analysis.evidence: In מַה זֹּאת עָשִׂית, “What is this you have done?”, מַה asks the woman to identify her deed. She names it in her reply וָאֹכֵל, “and I ate.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected interrogative pronoun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God asks the woman מַה זֹּאת עָשִׂית, “What is this you have done?” Her reply וָאֹכֵל, “and I ate,” identifies the act.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, second person feminine singular

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular verb agrees with its subject הָאִשָּׁה, “the woman,” and introduces her reply הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי וָאֹכֵל, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַתֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁה, “the woman said,” the noun identifies the speaker as the woman God has just addressed in לָאִשָּׁה.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: In הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי (“the serpent deceived me”), the woman identifies the serpent as the one who deceived her. The definite article refers back to the serpent that spoke to her.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state with the definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: The woman names הַנָּחָשׁ (“the serpent”) as the subject. The suffix ־נִי refers to the woman herself. She explains why she ate: “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third masculine singular, with a first common singular object suffix.

analysis.evidence: The woman says הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי, “the serpent deceived me,” then gives her own action in the first person, וָאֹכֵל, “and I ate.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, first person common singular, with prefixed וָ־.
